question: A collector had 174 cards initially. They removed 44 for trading. They added 32 from a purchase. They divided by 2 for album organization. They multiplied by 7 for complete sets. Each card cost 5 cents. How many cards did they have in complete sets?

A fund started with 127 dollars donated. They added 19 dollars Monday. They added 61 dollars Tuesday. They multiplied by 4 through grant matching. They added 45 dollars from a raffle. They added 8 more dollars from tips. They removed 666 for charity work. The organization employed 5 people. How much money remained in the fund?

A warehouse started with 217 boxes Monday morning. They removed 150 boxes for shipment. They removed 64 more for another order. They divided remaining by 3 for store distribution. They added 17 boxes from a return shipment. The facility operated 24 hours daily. How many boxes did each store receive?

A craft store had 68 supplies initially. They added 75 more from a supplier. They multiplied by 5 for class kits. They multiplied by 5 again for bulk sale. They multiplied by 9 for regional stores. They added 6 items from clearance. The manager opened the shop 7 days a week. How many craft supplies were sold?

A factory produced 56 units initially. They multiplied by 7 for the week's quota. They added 30 more from bonus production. They removed 328 for a canceled order. They added 7 units from a recount. They multiplied by 2 for packaging. They added 19 to gift orders. The facility had 20 workers. How many units were packaged?

A restaurant had 64 meals prepared initially. They added 48 more from kitchen production. They multiplied by 3 for lunch service. They divided by 3 for portion control. They added 36 more from dinner prep. The kitchen served 12 hours daily. How many meals were ready to serve?

A business had 191 units starting. They added 48 more through production. They removed 89 for customer orders. They removed 149 for returns. They multiplied by 4 for repackaging. They added 66 from a supplier shipment. Sarah had worked there 3 years. How many units were in inventory?

A factory produced 202 units initially. They multiplied by 9 through first shift. They multiplied by 9 again for second shift. They added 39 from bonus production. They removed 5485 for a large order. The facility operated on a 16-hour schedule. How many units remained?

A school had 101 students initially. They added 33 new students fall semester. They added 34 new students spring. They added 67 from transfer students. They multiplied by 5 for class sections. They removed 81 who graduated early. The building had 50 classrooms. How many student-sections were created?

A store had 234 items on Monday. They added 6 items from restocking. They added 77 more items Tuesday. They removed 171 items for clearance. They added 24 items from a delivery. They multiplied by 7 for the week's supply. The manager worked 40-hour weeks. How many items were stocked?

A coach had 115 equipment pieces initially. He divided by 5 for team distribution. He added 3 more from storage. He added 79 items from a donation. He removed 94 damaged items. He multiplied by 6 for seasonal expansion. His assistant earned 20 dollars per hour. How many equipment pieces remained?

A student had 26 coins initially. She added 41 more through saving. She removed 56 for a purchase. She multiplied by 4 through allowance. She divided by 2 for sharing. She divided by 2 again. She removed 8 for charity. The school day lasted 7 hours. How many coins remained?

A business had 205 items in storage. They added 15 more from suppliers. They multiplied by 2 for packaging. They removed 323 damaged items. They removed 111 for a clearance sale. They added 65 from a delivery. They added 68 from returns. The warehouse was 5000 square feet. How many items remained?

A gardener started with 61 plants initially. She removed 29 to replant elsewhere. She added 64 new seedlings. She divided by 4 for garden sections. She multiplied by 4 for potting. She added 80 more from the nursery. The garden got 8 hours of sun daily. How many plants did she end up with?

A factory produced 123 units initially. They multiplied by 5 for a large order. They removed 432 units for returns. They multiplied by 4 for packaging lots. They removed 589 for a canceled contract. They removed 88 more in adjustments. They removed 34 for quality control. The facility had 25 workers. How many units remained?

A carpenter started with 138 pieces initially. He removed 13 damaged pieces. He multiplied by 9 for a custom project. He removed 393 pieces for another job. He added 52 pieces from salvage. He removed 201 pieces for storage. Converting to hours of work costs money. How many pieces did he have?

A bakery had 142 loaves of bread. They multiplied by 4 for a catering order. They removed 506 loaves for a bulk purchase. They multiplied by 4 for regional distribution. They added 47 from night baking. His manager oversaw 15 staff members. How many loaves did they distribute?

A baker had 37 pastries to start. She added 35 more from morning baking. She multiplied by 7 for gift boxes. She divided by 3 for portion control. She removed 32 for a special order. The shop opened 7 days a week. How many pastries were sold?

A gardener had 74 seeds initially. She removed 12 damaged seeds. She removed 39 more for sorting. She added 47 new seeds. She added 48 more seeds. She added 53 from a friend's garden. She multiplied by 9 for planting rows. The garden was 10 by 10 feet. How many rows of seeds?

A warehouse had 181 items initially. They removed 20 for an urgent order. They added 15 from a restock. They removed 38 for quality checks. They removed 101 for distribution. They multiplied by 8 for packaging lots. The facility had 30 employees. How many packaged items?

A warehouse had 209 boxes initially. They removed 134 for delivery. They divided by 3 for three stores. They multiplied by 2 for both seasons. They added 66 more from suppliers. The manager earned 20 dollars hourly. How many boxes did each store get?

A business had 199 units starting out. They added 72 more from production. They multiplied by 3 for packaging. They multiplied by 2 for distribution lots. They added 15 for bonus items. The company employed 10 people. How many units were shipped?

A student had 19 books initially. She added 73 more from the library. She removed 32 for classroom use. She added 68 for a project. She added 21 more from purchases. She added 26 for a book club. The school library had 1000 books. How many books did she have?

A coach had 84 supplies starting. He multiplied by 2 for team needs. He removed 150 old items. He added 15 from donations. He added 44 new supplies. Converting to hours of storage costs money. How many supplies remained?

A collector had 138 coins initially. He added 68 more from purchases. He multiplied by 9 for the rare set. He removed 822 damaged coins. He removed 1023 for selling. His friend had 50 coins. How many coins did he keep?
